newsitem.title: UK: Chinese cigarette sales rise despite govmt ad ban.
newsitem.headline: Chinese cigarette sales rise despite govmt ad ban.

text.p: Western cigarette manufacturers are still promoting their brands in China despite tough government measures to try and curtail tobacco consumption said a report issued on Monday by market research company, Euromonitor.

The report indicates that despite the best efforts of the government, the Chinese are smoking more than ever before. Consumers smoked an average of ten cigarettes a day in 1994 but this has risen to 14 a day this year.

The majority of smokers are male but women are taking up the habit. About six per cent of the female population smokes but that represents an increase of 13 per cent on 1992 figures. The report said that over the past two years the Chinese government has banned all tobacco advertising and demanded that manufacturers must devote ten per cent of the front of the packaging to a government health warning.
However, foreign tobacco companies are circumventing the rules by sponsoring sports such as the China car rally and the Chinese football league.
China's most popular cigarette brand is Hong Ta Shan made by the Yuxi cigarette factory. Of the available foreign brands Philip Morris-owned Marlboro is the most popular.

While there is a growing market for Western cigarette brands - imports grew by 209 per cent between 1992 and 1996 - many of them are smuggled into the country from Hong Kong, the Philippines and Korea.
